# nish/crypto/sha512

SHA-512 and SHA-384, written from FIPS 180-4.

```ts
import {
  SHA384_SIZE,
  SHA512_BLOCK,
  SHA512_SIZE,
  Sha384,
  Sha512,
  sha384,
  sha512,
} from "nish/crypto/sha512";
```

```ts
import { sha512, sha384, Sha512 } from "nish/crypto/sha512";

const whole: u8[] = sha512(message); // 64 bytes; sha384 answers 48

const h = new Sha512();
h.update(first, 0, toI32(first.length));
h.update(second, 0, toI32(second.length));
const all: u8[] = h.digest();
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="sha384" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#sha384">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="sha512" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#sha512">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Sha384" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#sha384-1">

<scalar-card title="Sha512" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#sha512-1">

<scalar-detail title="One engine, two hashes">

Both hashes are one compression function over
eight 64-bit words: SHA-384 starts from its own initial value (§5.3.4) and
keeps the first 48 bytes of the result (§6.5), SHA-512 starts from §5.3.5 and
keeps all 64. So one engine does the work, and `Sha512` and `Sha384` are the
two ways to start it.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Time says only the length">

A hasher streams: `update` any number of
windows, `copy` to take an independent hasher at the same point (TLS 1.3
hashes its transcript and reads intermediate hashes of it), then `digest`
once. The work depends on how many bytes arrive and never on their values:
there is no branch and no table index on message data, so a secret message
(an HMAC key, a transcript) is hashed in time that says nothing about it but
its length.

</scalar-detail>

The constants are the fractional parts of the cube roots of the first eighty
primes (§4.2.3) and of the square roots of the first sixteen (§5.3.4, §5.3.5),
as FIPS 180-4 defines them. A literal past 2^53 cannot be written exactly, so
each is spelled as its two 32-bit halves.

## Functions

### sha384

The SHA-384 digest of all of `data`, as a fresh 48-byte array. An array
longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes panics, as in `sha512`.

```ts
function sha384(data: u8[]): u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The whole message; it is read, not changed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

A fresh 48-byte digest.

</scalar-field>

### sha512

The SHA-512 digest of all of `data`, as a fresh 64-byte array. An array
longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes panics, for the reason `sha256` gives: a longer
length does not survive `toI32` under `--number-mode f64`, and the digest
would be of a prefix.

```ts
function sha512(data: u8[]): u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The whole message; it is read, not changed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

A fresh 64-byte digest.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### Sha384

A streaming SHA-384 hasher, with `Sha512`'s methods. `digest` answers a
fresh 48-byte array.

```ts
class Sha384
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Sha384()` | A hasher at the start of an empty message (FIPS 180-4 §5.3.4's initial hash value). |
| `engine: Sha512Engine` | The engine the hash runs on. `nish/crypto/hmac` and `nish/crypto/ed25519` reach into it to wipe a hasher, and the tests to check the wipe; a caller has no use for it. |
| `copy(): Sha384` | An independent hasher at the same point: updating either leaves the other alone. |
| `digest(): u8[]` | Pads the message (§5.1.2) and answers its digest, the first 48 bytes of the final hash value (§6.5). Ends the computation: a second `digest` panics. |
| `update(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Absorbs `data[off .. off + len)`. A window outside `data`, or an update after `digest`, panics. |

### Sha512

A streaming SHA-512 hasher. `update` takes a window `(data, off, len)`;
`digest` answers a fresh 64-byte array, after which the hasher is spent and
another `update` or `digest` panics.

```ts
class Sha512
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Sha512()` | A hasher at the start of an empty message (FIPS 180-4 §5.3.5's initial hash value). |
| `engine: Sha512Engine` | The engine the hash runs on. `nish/crypto/hmac` and `nish/crypto/ed25519` reach into it to wipe a hasher, and the tests to check the wipe; a caller has no use for it. |
| `copy(): Sha512` | An independent hasher at the same point: updating either leaves the other alone. |
| `digest(): u8[]` | Pads the message (§5.1.2) and answers its digest. Ends the computation: a second `digest` panics. |
| `update(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Absorbs `data[off .. off + len)`. A window outside `data`, or an update after `digest`, panics. |
